ABOUT THE ROLE
Perplexity's security team protects products used by millions of people and thousands of enterprises, including AI agents that browse the web, run code, and act in customer systems. The team is small, senior, and builds most of what it uses: our own detections, agents that triage and investigate alerts around the clock, continuous offensive testing, and secure-by-default platforms for the rest of engineering.
We're also turning what we've built into cybersecurity products for customers, so the same team that defends Perplexity builds what we ship.
We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead and grow Security Engineering, including the engineers building our cybersecurity products. You'll own the team's execution and people, set the technical direction for how we defend our infrastructure, products, and corporate environment, and lead the product engineering work that brings those systems to customers. You'll stay close enough to the work to run an incident or review a design yourself. You'll report to Perplexity's head of security and work with engineering, infrastructure, IT, product, legal, and our co-founders.
RESPONSIBILITIES
- Lead, hire, and grow a team of security engineers across detection and response, cloud and infrastructure security, application and product security, offensive security, and identity and corporate security.
- Lead the engineers building our cybersecurity products: set technical direction for agent-driven products across application security, offensive testing, cloud security, and detection and response, and own delivery to design partners and enterprise customers.
- Keep the internal security program and the product tightly linked, so what the team runs on Perplexity every day becomes what we ship, and customer feedback improves how we defend ourselves.
- Set the roadmap for Security Engineering, balancing incident load, risk reduction, and long-term platform investments, and make clear prioritization calls.
- Own security incident response operations: on-call health, escalation, cross-team coordination during incidents, and postmortems that lead to real fixes.
- Drive an AI-first security program. Push the team to automate investigation, response, and remediation with agents, and hold that automation to a high bar for accuracy and safety.
- Partner with engineering and infrastructure leaders to get security work into their roadmaps, from threat models and design reviews to least-privilege access and secure-by-default libraries.
- Represent Security Engineering in enterprise customer security reviews, external researcher and bug bounty engagements, and audits.
- Build the team's operating rhythm: clear ownership, metrics that matter (time to detect, time to contain, open risk), and written standards others can follow.
- Stay hands-on: review designs and code, run investigations when needed, and keep a working understanding of the systems the team defends.
QUALIFICATIONS
- 8+ years of engineering experience in security, with at least 3 years managing security or infrastructure engineering teams.
- Deep hands-on background in at least two of: detection and response, cloud security (AWS preferred), application or product security, offensive security, or identity and access management.
- Experience leading incident response for serious security incidents, including technical investigation, containment, and communication with executives and customers.
- Strong management practice: clear feedback, effective 1:1s, career development, and a track record of hiring and retaining strong senior engineers.
- Comfortable with modern infrastructure (Kubernetes, cloud-native services, CI/CD) and able to engage credibly with engineers on design and code.
- Ability to make good tradeoffs under pressure and explain risk clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
- Experience shipping software products to external customers, ideally security products, including working with design partners and turning customer feedback into a roadmap.
- Experience building security programs at a fast-growing company, where you built more than you bought.
- Bonus: experience securing AI/ML systems, LLM applications, or autonomous agents, or using AI to scale security operations.
- Bonus: experience supporting enterprise compliance programs (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP) from the engineering side.

We build and run the inference engine behind every Perplexity query and deploy dozens of model architectures at scale with tight latency and cost budgets. Our stack is Rust, Python, CUDA, and CuTe DSL - and we need another engineer to join us.
WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON
Examples of real work the team does:
- New models support. Support transformer-based retrieval, text-generation, and multimodal models in our inference infrastructure, from weight loading, request scheduling and KV-cache management to support in API Gateway.
- GPU kernels migration to CuTe DSL. Port our in-house CUDA kernels to NVIDIA's CuTe DSL so they run on GB200 today and are portable to Vera Rubin racks tomorrow.
- Rust-native serving runtime. Develop our internal Rust-based inference server to solve all Python pains and keep up with rapidly growing traffic.
- Performance optimisation. Profile and fix bottlenecks from network ingress through continuous batching and GPU kernel interleaving.
- Reliability and observability. Build dashboards, alerts, and automated remediation so we catch regressions before users do. Respond to and learn from production incidents.
WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- Deep experience with GPU programming and performance work (CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS, or similar). Any other deep systems programming experience is a plus.
- You understand modern LLM architectures and are able to bring them up reliably in a production environment.
- You've built and operated production distributed systems under real load - ideally performance-critical ones.
- Comfortable working across languages and layers: Rust for the serving runtime, Python for model code, CUDA/CuteDSL for kernels.
- You own problems end-to-end. You can read a research paper on Monday, write a kernel on Wednesday, and debug a production incident on Friday.
- Self-directed. You do well in fast-moving environments where the path forward isn't laid out for you.
GOOD IF YOU TOUCHED ANY OF
- ML compilers and framework internals: PyTorch internals, torch.compile, custom operators.
- Distributed GPU communication: NCCL, NVLink, InfiniBand, RDMA libraries, model/tensor parallelism.
- Low-precision inference: INT8/FP8/FP4 quantization, mixed-precision serving.
- Profiling and debugging tools: Nsight Compute/Systems, CUDA-GDB, PTX/SASS analysis.
- Container orchestration: Kubernetes, GPU scheduling, autoscaling inference workloads.
QUALIFICATIONS
- 3+ years of professional software engineering experience with meaningful work on ML inference or high-performance systems.
- Familiarity with at least one deep learning framework (PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow).
- Understanding of GPU architectures (memory hierarchy, warp scheduling, tensor cores).
- Understanding of common LLM architectures and inference optimization techniques (e.g. quantization, speculative decoding, prefill-decode disaggregation).

ABOUT THE ROLE
The Enterprise Knowledge Platform team builds the data and action layer that connects Perplexity's agents to the systems where enterprise work happens. Useful agents need more than access to APIs: they need to discover the right tools, understand an organization's data and terminology, and act reliably within its permissions. This team brings native connectors, MCP servers, and CLI-backed tools into a consistent platform, and builds the marketplace through which customers adopt integrations and partners extend the ecosystem.
This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from designing connector infrastructure and semantic models to shipping the experiences customers use to discover, connect, and activate integrations. You'll build the runtime that executes tool calls, the knowledge layer that makes enterprise context reusable across connectors, and the developer and marketplace foundations that help the ecosystem grow. Working with AI Research and Enterprise teams, you'll turn fragmented systems into reliable, permission-aware capabilities that agents can use to complete real work. The impact is direct: every improvement helps customers put their existing software and knowledge to work through Perplexity.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Own the connector runtime that registers, hosts, and executes native connectors, hosted MCP servers, and CLI-backed tools through a consistent agent-facing interface.
- Build the semantic and knowledge layer, including tool and entity schemas, capability metadata, relationships, organization-specific terminology, and reusable corrections, while preserving provenance and source-system permissions.
- Design discovery, search, and recommendation systems that help agents find relevant tools and context and help users and organizations choose integrations that fit their work.
- Build the marketplace and activation experience end to end, from browsing and recommendations to installation, configuration, admin enablement, and ongoing adoption.
- Make connector execution reliable and observable, with structured results, retries, idempotency, pagination, rate-limit handling, and recovery from partial failures. Own reliability targets, production monitoring, and incident response.
- Implement connector authentication, credential isolation, and permission enforcement, partnering with Trust & Governance, Security, and Backend Platform on shared policies and tenant boundaries.
- Build the onboarding and publishing path for internal teams and external partners, including schemas, test fixtures, validation, review, and versioning.
QUALIFICATIONS
- 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.
- Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable platforms that integrate heterogeneous APIs and services with clear security and isolation boundaries.
- Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS and Kubernetes.
- Deep expertise in at least one of the following:
- Connector runtimes, API platforms, or MCP servers, including authentication and authorization.
- Schema design, semantic modeling, or knowledge systems that capture relationships and organizational context.
- Search, ranking, recommendation, or tool discovery systems.
- Marketplaces, developer platforms, or enterprise onboarding and activation experiences.
- Ability to work across backend infrastructure and customer-facing product experiences, translating complex integration requirements into clear APIs, developer tools, and intuitive workflows.
- Sound technical judgment in security-sensitive, distributed systems, balancing credential isolation, permission correctness, and failure behavior with performance, usability, and delivery speed.
- A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through adoption, setting technical direction for shared platforms, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.
If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every qualification. We value demonstrated impact, deep ownership, and the initiative to turn ambiguity into results.

Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads.
RESPONSIBILITIES
- Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure.
- Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs.
- Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints.
- Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet.
- Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run.
- Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention.
- Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap.
QUALIFICATIONS
We expect you to have real depth in most of these:
- Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply.
- You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE).
- You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is.
- Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load.
- You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++.
- You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions.
- You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.
ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE
- Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.
- Slurm or other HPC schedulers.
- GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable.
- High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production.
- Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast.
RESPONSIBILITIES
- Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost.
- Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load.
- Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers.
- Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested.
- Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back.

- Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice.
- Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure.
- Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team.
QUALIFICATIONS
We expect you to have real depth in most of these:
- Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them.
- Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count.

- You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it.
- Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter.
- A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes.
- You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.
ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE
- Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets.
- Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF.

Perplexity is looking for a Content Designer to shape the words across our products. You'll design the language people see and hear across our family of Perplexity apps, from the first screen of onboarding to the way an agent explains what it's doing. Fundamentally, we are all writers. Our product is primarily spoken language and written product; but as we scale, we want someone who will continue to work on clarity, usefulness, and keep it unmistakably Perplexity.
You're a designer first? You're an engineer first? You're a writer first? Your shape is not conventional, and you wear many hats. You are fluent in AI tooling. You have strong UX fundamentals and good product instincts. You use language to solve product problems: flows, naming, information architecture, error states, permissions, and moments where people need to trust what the product is telling them. You command words. You command agents, and make decisions about words. You can write one perfect line, and you can build the system that keeps thousands of lines consistent.
You'll sit on the Design Systems team and work closely with product designers, engineers, PMs, research, brand, and marketing. (Again) You're fluent in AI-powered tools and use it every day. You understand how models behave, how prompts and system instructions shape what people see, and how to define and judge quality when the output isn't fully deterministic.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Design and write in-product language across web, mobile, desktop, and voice, including UI copy, flows, onboarding, notifications, empty states, errors, and in-product education
- Partner with product designers from the start of a project, shaping flows, structure, and information architecture as well as the words in them
- Name features and products, and own terminology, navigation labels, and taxonomies so the product stays easy to understand as it grows
- Make complex AI and agent behavior understandable, including what the product is doing, why, what it can't do, and when it needs a person's input
- Shape how AI-generated content reads by writing and refining prompts and system instructions, and help define voice and response style for our models in product
- Define content quality standards and help build evaluation criteria, datasets, and reviewer guidance for AI-generated content
- Build and maintain voice and tone guidelines, content patterns, and content guidance in our design system so every team can write well
- Use research, data, and experiments to test language and improve comprehension, activation, and task completion
- Partner with brand and marketing so product language and our external voice feel like one company
- Work with internationalization partners so the product reads well in every language we support
- Review copy in code and ship small language changes directly when it's the fastest path
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- 5+ years of experience in content design, UX writing, or product design, shipping software at scale
- An excellent portfolio that shows how your language shaped product decisions, with clear before and after examples and your role in each
- Strong UX fundamentals, including interaction design, information architecture, usability, and accessibility
- Good product sensibility and judgment about what to build, what to cut, and what matters most to people
- Exceptional writing and editing skills, with range from precise interface copy to clear explanations and confident naming
- Strong AI fluency, including hands-on experience writing prompts, working with LLMs, and judging the quality of AI-generated content
- Systems thinking, with experience building content frameworks, style guides, or terminology that scale across teams
- Clear communication, with the ability to explain content decisions and tradeoffs to designers, engineers, and leaders
- You care about shipping great software more than anything else
NICE TO HAVE
- Experience designing content for AI products, assistants, agents, or conversational interfaces
- Experience with prompt engineering, model evals, or working with research teams on model behavior
- Experience across consumer and enterprise products, including admin, permissions, privacy, and billing flows
- Comfort working in code, such as editing strings, reviewing PRs, or prototyping with AI tools
- Experience with localization and writing for global audiences
NOTES FOR CANDIDATES
We want to see portfolio work where your words changed the product. Show us the problem, the options you explored, the language you shipped, and what happened after. We value end-to-end ownership, range, and impact, and we'd love to see examples of AI-related work, such as prompts, evaluations, or content you designed for model output.

In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people and teams adopt Perplexity and Computer on their own, and the Growth team owns the loops that turn that adoption into lasting usage and revenue.
We're hiring a Growth GTM Engineer to build the systems that turn product usage into revenue and turn self-serve usage into enterprise pipeline. You'll turn first-party Computer and Enterprise usage into account-level signals. You'll ship the in-product paths that capture sales intent, and build and validate those signals with data science. Alongside product engineers, you ship production code, instrument the product and run experiments. You'll partner closely with Revenue Operations, who own Salesforce, CPQ, routing and sales reporting.
Tech Stack: TypeScript | Next.js | React | Python | PostgreSQL | Snowflake | Eppo | AWS
WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT
- Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.
- Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.
- Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.
- Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.
- Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Build account-level PLG signals: map users and workspaces to accounts, and define the activation, expansion and intent signals that predict an enterprise deal. Publish them as trusted models that sales use for scoring and routing.
- Own the in-product paths from self-serve to sales, like contact-sales entry points, high-intent upsells and meeting booking, across web and app. Decide who sees them, when and with what context, and measure them end to end, from surface to booked meeting to pipeline.
- Lead experiments end to end on sales-assist surfaces and targeting, from hypothesis and instrumentation through analysis and rollout. Partner with Data Science to measure meetings and qualified opportunities, not just clicks.
- Build the internal tools and automation Growth and GTM teams run on
- Partner closely with Sales, Sales Systems, Data Science, Marketing and Product to turn product signals into pipeline. Be upstream partner to sales systems that own Salesforce, CPQ and routing
QUALIFICATIONS
- 2+ years as a growth, GTM, data or full-stack engineer, shipping production code (TypeScript/React, Python).
- Strong SQL and comfort building data models in a warehouse (Snowflake, dbt-style).
- Experience instrumenting product events and running A/B experiments end to end.
- Commercial instinct: you start from a revenue problem ("trial-to-enterprise conversion won't move") and work back to the signal or surface that fixes it.
- Comfort with REST APIs, webhooks and integrating third-party GTM tools.
- Operator mindset: you talk to customers directly, ship fixes, and don't need a PM to translate requests.
NICE TO HAVE
- Experience in a PLG-to-enterprise motion: product-qualified leads, scoring users into accounts, sales-assist flows.
- Experience as a GTM or growth engineer at a B2B SaaS or GTM-tooling company.
- Entity resolution, dedup or domain enrichment.
- Familiarity with Salesforce, Default, Chili Piper, Intercom, Clay, Hightouch/Polytomic or similar (as a consumer and integrator, not an admin).
- Experience building LLM-powered internal tools or agents.

Perplexity is seeking an intrepid Member of Technical Staff to take on one of the AI industry's most unique engineering roles. You'll work directly with Perplexity's senior leadership to spearhead a broad portfolio of strategic technology initiatives across policy, law, operations, and corporate affairs.
As a Member of Technical Staff in the Policy & Strategic Initiatives group, you'll occupy a front-row seat to the foremost policy issues animating the AI ecosystem. You'll also get a panoptic view of how leading AI companies operate, make decisions, and engage with broader society.
Those seeking to marry technical expertise and broader interests in law, policy, and corporate affairs will find a home in this role. You'll make contributions to Perplexity that defy traditional boundaries, with a bench of mentors who will push you to learn and grow day after day.
WHAT YOU'LL DO:
Your work will be both highly interdisciplinary and firmly grounded in engineering rigor. On any given day, you might:
- Harness AI agents to research high-stakes policy and regulatory issues pertaining to Perplexity.
- Build automated platforms for harvesting, prioritizing, and patenting Perplexity's inventions, in collaboration with our AI researchers and intellectual property attorneys.
- Work hands-on with our Legal team and outside counsel in support of high-tech litigation matters in U.S. federal court.
- Engineer privacy and compliance systems that efficiently scale with our growing portfolio of frontier AI products (such as Comet https://www.perplexity.ai/comet and Computer https://www.perplexity.ai/products/computer).
- Contribute to regulatory filings and responses that require impeccable command of AI technology, Perplexity's own systems, and the broader policy landscape.
- Embed with our People team to implement first-party software solutions for recruiting, labor compliance, and performance management.
- Participate in meetings with Capitol Hill, executive branch officials, international partners, and civil society as a subject-matter expert on both AI technology and policy.
The above is a small sampling of activities; no two days will be the same, and your work will take you to all corners of our company. You'll interact each day with Perplexity's senior leaders, who will come to rely on you as a creative problem solver for simple and complex matters alike.
WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:
No single profile defines our ideal candidate for this role. Here are some examples of people who might thrive here:
- Exceptionally talented early-career engineers (new grads welcome) who are (1) well-read in law, tech policy, or economics, and (2) wish to grow in both technical and non-technical disciplines.
- We welcome candidates who plan to attend law school or PhD programs in the future; we ask for a minimum 2-year commitment (i.e., you would apply for the entering class of 2028 or later).
- Experienced engineers at top tech companies who wish to develop policy, business, and operations chops.
- Lawyers or economists (new JD or PhD grads welcome) who've kept their engineering skills sharp and are excited to reimagine their fields in the age of AI.
- This is a non-exhaustive list; other profiles may also be great fits.
No matter which profile describes you, we'll also be looking for:
- Evidence of exceptional ability and 99th-percentile work ethic.
- Strong technical skills at or above Perplexity's hiring bar for software engineers.
- Fluency with frontier intelligence tools (such as Perplexity Computer https://www.perplexity.ai/products/computer).
- High intrinsically-enforced standards for the craft and quality of your work.
- Strong communication and writing skills, ideally demonstrated via samples of past written work product.
- Curiosity and excitement about new and unfamiliar fields; eagerness to redefine your job every 3-6 months.
- Ability to quickly dive deep in any given field and develop mastery rivaling that of domain experts.
- Unimpeachable judgment, integrity, and discretion to be entrusted with the company's most important matters.
- A service-oriented attitude that continually questions how company systems and processes might better serve stakeholders.

In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people and teams adopt Perplexity and Computer on their own, and our marketing programs bring in thousands more leads. To turn that demand into pipeline, every lead has to be enriched, scored, and routed to the right next step within minutes.
We're hiring a Growth GTM Engineer on the Revenue Operations team to own the lead-to-engagement engine. You'll orchestrate enrichment across marketing and product leads.
You'll build the scoring models that combine firmographic and technographic fit with demonstrated intent and product behavior. You'll own the routing that sends each lead back to Marketing for nurture or to BDRs and Sales for engagement. And you'll help build the custom internal apps our reps use to research, prioritize and engage prospects.
You'll report to the Head of Marketing Operations, who sets the priorities for this work and owns our marketing automation platform, campaigns and attribution.
You'll write production code, own the data and logic between our warehouse and Salesforce, and measure everything you build against meetings, pipeline and revenue.
Tech stack: Salesforce | Snowflake | dbt | Python | TypeScript | Clay | Reverse ETL (Hightouch or similar) | Routing and scheduling (Default, Chili Piper or similar) | LLM APIs
WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT
- Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.
- Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.
- Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.
- Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.
- Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Own enrichment orchestration. Design and run waterfall enrichment across third-party data providers, AI research agents and first-party data for every marketing and product lead. Handle lead-to-account matching, deduplication, field governance, data freshness and provider cost, so every record is complete, accurate and ready to act on.
- Own and iterate on lead and account scoring. Build fit models from firmographic and technographic attributes such as industry, size, region, tech stack, AI maturity and buying-committee coverage. Combine them with intent and behavior signals: web and content engagement, email and campaign engagement from Marketing Operations, third-party intent, event activity, and product usage signals from the Growth team. Calibrate the models against closed-won and closed-lost data, version them, and explain to Sales why a lead scored the way it did.
- Own lead routing. Design the decision logic that sends each lead to Marketing for nurture or to a BDR, AE or Account Manager for engagement, based on score, segment, territory, account ownership, capacity and existing opportunities. Co-define lifecycle stages, handoff SLAs, recycle rules and speed-to-lead triggers with the Head of Marketing Operations, and enforce them in Salesforce and our routing tools.
- Close the feedback loop. Instrument the funnel from lead creation to MQL, meeting, opportunity and closed-won. Find where leads stall, which sources and signals predict pipeline, and whether our qualification criteria still hold, then send those insights back into scoring, routing and Marketing programs. Supply the data behind attribution, which the Head of Marketing Operations owns.
- Help build custom internal apps for prospect engagement. Ship the tools reps use every day, such as account and prospect research briefs, signal-triggered alerts in Slack and Salesforce, prioritized call and outreach queues, and LLM-powered agents that draft personalized outreach and prepare reps before first touch. Run them like products: talk to users, track adoption and retire what doesn't get used. These apps are part of our BDR prospecting toolset, a combination of internal builds and vendor solutions that the Head of Marketing Operations owns or co-owns. Deliver against that roadmap, including integrating vendor tools with Salesforce and our data layer.
- Be the technical owner of the lead data layer. Build and maintain the dbt models, reverse ETL syncs, APIs and webhooks that connect Snowflake, Salesforce, marketing automation, enrichment providers and engagement tools. Make sure data flows are observable, tested and trusted. Support the rollout of our first marketing automation platform by building the Salesforce and warehouse side of its sync.
- Partner across the business. Work with Marketing, Growth, BDR and Sales leadership, Data Science and Sales Systems to turn messy processes into durable systems. Work with the Growth team, using the PLG signals they publish to drive scoring and routing.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
In your first 30 days:
- Audit the current enrichment coverage, scoring logic, routing rules and lead SLAs, and document the gaps that cost us pipeline.
In your first 90 days:
- Ship an enrichment waterfall with measurable gains in fill rate and accuracy.
- Ship an evolution of our unified scoring model that combines fit, intent and product signals, with a published rubric Sales trusts.
- Ship routing that sends every lead to nurture or sales within an agreed SLA, with dashboards that show speed to lead and conversion by route.
In your first 6 months:
- Ship at least one rep-facing engagement app or agent with sustained weekly use by BDRs and AEs.
- Show a measurable lift in MQL-to-meeting and meeting-to-opportunity conversion.
QUALIFICATIONS
- 4+ years in GTM engineering, RevOps or Marketing Ops engineering, growth engineering, or data engineering in a B2B SaaS environment, including at least 2 years building enrichment, scoring or routing systems.
- Commercial instinct. You start from a revenue problem, like "inbound enterprise leads wait too long for a first touch," and work back to the data, logic or tool that fixes it.
- Strong SQL and experience building data models in a warehouse (Snowflake, dbt or similar). You pull your own data.
- Production code in Python or TypeScript. You've shipped internal tools, integrations or agents that real users depend on.
- Deep working knowledge of the Salesforce data model (leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities, campaigns, ownership), and experience automating within it and integrating with it.
- Hands-on experience with enrichment and intent providers and orchestration tools, such as Clay, ZoomInfo, Apollo, Clearbit, 6sense, Demandbase or Common Room.
- Fluency with funnel mechanics: lead lifecycle design, scoring models, routing and assignment logic, SLAs, attribution data and conversion metrics.
- Comfort with REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth, rate limits and error handling across third-party GTM tools.
- Operator and business partner mindset. You work directly with reps and marketers, ship fixes quickly, and don't need a PM to translate requests.
NICE TO HAVE
- Experience in a hybrid PLG and sales-led motion: product-qualified leads, mapping users to accounts, and sales-assist routing.
- Experience with routing and scheduling tools (Default, Chili Piper, LeanData) and reverse ETL (Hightouch, Census, Polytomic).
- Experience building LLM-powered research, personalization or qualification agents, including evaluation and monitoring.
- Experience with statistical or ML-based scoring (logistic regression, gradient boosting) and model calibration.
- Entity resolution and domain-matching experience at scale.
- Prior GTM Engineer experience at a GTM-tooling or AI-native company.
